title: spend: deterministic, canonical input construction

traits.evidence: liana/src/spend.rs select_coins_for_spend: `let mut v = candidate_coins.to_vec(); v.sort_unstable_by_key(|c| c.outpoint);`. Inputs are pushed in selector.selected_indices() order (BTreeSet = candidate index order), so input order becomes outpoint order.

traits.before: random per run (candidates come from a HashMap)
traits.evidence: PR body: 'candidates come from a HashMap, so tie-breaking (and input order) was random per run, sort by outpoint.'

summary: Liana's spend and recovery transactions would order inputs by outpoint and pick coins deterministically, where today input order and tie-breaking follow random HashMap iteration.
notes: Written by bc1cindy as a follow-up to rust-payjoin#1597. rust-bitcoin's OutPoint ordering compares the txid's internal byte order, not the reversed display order BIP-69 uses, so this is outpoint-sorted but not strictly BIP-69. It also adds a coin_to_psbt_input helper, which leaves nSequence (0xFFFFFFFD) unchanged.

title: [WIP] Payjoin receiver

traits.evidence: lianad/src/payjoin/receiver.rs contribute_inputs: `proposal.try_preserving_privacy(candidate_inputs.clone()).unwrap_or(candidate_inputs.next()...)`
lianad/src/payjoin/receiver.rs: candidates are built in `HashMap::<OutPoint, (Coin, TxIn, Input, Weight)>` and passed on as `candidate_inputs_map.values()`
lianad/src/payjoin/receiver.rs: `db_conn.coins(&[CoinStatus::Confirmed], &[])`

summary: Liana gains a BIP77 payjoin receiver that adds one confirmed wallet coin to the sender's transaction, picked by try_preserving_privacy from a HashMap-ordered candidate list.
notes: Receiver-only path. WIP, not draft. If try_preserving_privacy fails, it falls back to the first HashMap candidate, which can break UIH avoidance. Outputs are committed without substituting the receiver script. The contributed input's nSequence is ENABLE_RBF_NO_LOCKTIME, and the payjoin lib coerces it to the sender's value. The catalog's Liana uih2/utxo_order values appear to come from this PR. Supersedes the 'DO NOT MERGE' POC #1806, which is not listed.

traits.before: one consolidating tx (all selected coins -> 1 output)
traits.evidence: liana-gui/src/app/state/spend/step.rs: `for (outpoint, feerate) in coin_feerates { daemon.create_spend_tx(&[outpoint], &HashMap::new(), feerate, None) }`

traits.after: per-tx random integer sat/vB in a user-set min/max range (opt-in)
traits.evidence: step.rs SweepRandomizeFees: `let feerate = min + (rand_val as u64 % range);` using liana::random::random_bytes()

summary: An opt-in GUI mode turns a multi-coin self-transfer into one single-input, single-output transaction per coin, each at a randomized whole-number feerate.
notes: Opt-in and GUI-only: the PR states 'No backend changes', so lianad's create_spend is unchanged. Feerates stay whole sat/vB numbers, so the round-feerate tell remains.

title: Payjoin-cli : add `--consolidate` mode

traits.evidence: payjoin-cli/src/app/v2/mod.rs & v1.rs: `let inputs = if consolidate.is_some() { wallet.select_receiver_utxos(consolidate)? ... } else { vec![proposal.try_preserving_privacy(candidate_inputs)?] }`
payjoin-cli/src/app/wallet.rs select_receiver_utxos: `unspent.sort_by_key(|utxo| Amount::from_btc(...)); unspent.drain(..smallest)`
payjoin-cli/src/cli/mod.rs: `#[arg(long = "consolidate", num_args = 0..=1, default_missing_value = "10")]`

summary: With the new opt-in --consolidate flag, the payjoin-cli receiver adds its N smallest UTXOs to the payjoin instead of one privacy-preserving input.
notes: Opt-in flag, receiver-only path, v1 and v2. Not a draft. The default path (one input via try_preserving_privacy) is unchanged. The PR says the input cap exists because of the BIP77 7088-byte proposal limit.

title: Payjoin-cli: add `--cut-through` mode

traits.after: multi-recipient (adds a forwarded third-party output with --cut-through)
traits.evidence: payjoin-cli/src/app/v2/mod.rs commit_outputs: `proposal.replace_receiver_outputs(vec![receiver_output.clone(), forward], &drain_script)`
payjoin-cli: `let inputs = if consolidate.is_some() || min_total > Amount::ZERO { wallet.select_receiver_utxos(consolidate, min_total)? ... }`

traits.after: smallest UTXOs for consolidation, then largest-first top-up until the forwarded amount is covered
traits.evidence: payjoin-cli/src/app/wallet.rs select_receiver_utxos: `while total < min_total { // Sorted ascending, so popping takes the largest remaining.`

summary: With the new opt-in --cut-through flag, the payjoin-cli receiver adds a third-party payment output to the payjoin and funds it with its own largest UTXOs.
notes: Opt-in flag, receiver-only path, draft. Stacked on #1878, so the diff includes --consolidate. On v1 with --cut-through, the receiver keeps its original output instead of substituting a fresh address (substitute_receiver_script is skipped). The author lists open TODOs, such as dropping FEE_HEADROOM_VB, so details may change.

title: Payjoin integration

traits.evidence: boltzr/src/payjoin/mod.rs select_contribution_input: `candidates.sort_by_key(|(amount, _)| *amount); for (_, input) in candidates { if receiver.clone().contribute_inputs(vec![input.clone()]).is_ok() { return Ok(input); } }`. try_preserving_privacy is never called.
boltzr/src/payjoin/mod.rs: wallet listunspent sorted ascending by amount, first fit wins
boltzr/src/payjoin/mod.rs: `btc_chain.list_unspent(None)` -> chain_client.rs `request_wallet(..., "listunspent", None)` (Core default minconf=1)

traits.after: lockup output = swap amount + contributed Boltz UTXO (oversized consolidation lockup)
traits.evidence: commit_outputs() without output substitution; contribute_inputs adds the input to the drain (lockup) output. The PR body says it allows 'the intentional oversized consolidation lockup'.

summary: On BTC->LN submarine swaps, Boltz would act as a payjoin receiver, adding its smallest UTXO that fits to the user's lockup transaction and folding that value into the swap lockup output.
notes: Draft, receiver-only path, lockup txs of BTC->LN submarine swaps only. The PR revives #892. Contributed inputs are signed by Core walletprocesspsbt, and the input type comes from the UTXO's address (P2WPKH/P2TR/other), not matched to the sender. The catalog's Boltz 'uih2_avoidance: yes' seems to come from an earlier revision (f3c117a) that used try_preserving_privacy. The current head (7a315f04) uses smallest-first first-fit.

title: feat: funding addresses

traits.evidence: boltz-core/src/bitcoin/tx.rs construct_raw: `-        version: Version::TWO,` / `+        // Use V3 transactions to enable zero-fee presigned funding-address transactions ... via TRUC relay.` / `+        version: Version(3),`

summary: Every Bitcoin claim and refund transaction built by Rust boltz-core's construct_raw would switch from nVersion 2 to nVersion 3 (TRUC), not only the new funding-address ones.
notes: Claim/refund/sweep only. Affects txs built by boltz-core Rust (boltzr swap claims via swap/manager.rs, the refund bumper, and new funding-address claims). TypeScript-side claims through the boltz-core npm package (Claim.ts) are not touched. The Liquid/elements tx.rs keeps its version. The PR has merge conflicts (last updated 2026-03-24), so the exact scope may change on rebase.
